headline: Messi and Salah face off as Argentina make three changes for Egypt clash
summary: Lionel Scaloni shifts the lineup for the World Cup round-of-16 match, bringing in Julian Alvarez, Nicolas Tagliafico, and Leandro Paredes.
details: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has made three key changes to the starting lineup for Tuesday's World Cup round-of-16 match against Egypt.
Striker Julian Alvarez replaces Lautaro Martinez in the attack, while Nicolas Tagliafico and Leandro Paredes return to the starting eleven.
Facundo Medina and Thiago Almada are the players who move to the bench for this high-stakes encounter.
On the Egyptian side, coach Hossam Hassan has made two adjustments to his squad, introducing forward Haissem Hassan and midfielder Mohanad Lashin.
Omar Marmoush and Hamdy Fathy have been replaced in Egypt's starting lineup as they look to challenge the South American giants.
The match features a highly anticipated clash between two of the world's best left-footed players, Lionel Messi and Mohamed Salah.
caption:

Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has made three key changes to the starting lineup for Tuesday's World Cup round-of-16 match against Egypt.

Striker Julian Alvarez replaces Lautaro Martinez in the attack, while Nicolas Tagliafico and Leandro Paredes return to the starting eleven.

Facundo Medina and Thiago Almada are the players who move to the bench for this high-stakes encounter.

On the Egyptian side, coach Hossam Hassan has made two adjustments to his squad, introducing forward Haissem Hassan and midfielder Mohanad Lashin.

Omar Marmoush and Hamdy Fathy have been replaced in Egypt's starting lineup as they look to challenge the South American giants.

The match features a highly anticipated clash between two of the world's best left-footed players, Lionel Messi and Mohamed Salah.

headline: 5.21 lakh govt posts remain vacant in Bangladesh
summary: State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari revealed the figures in parliament, outlining plans to fill the gaps with transparency and speed.
details: State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari informed parliament that 521,922 government service posts remain vacant as of June 30, 2025, while 1,464,350 officials are currently in service.

The minister detailed the vacancy status across different levels, noting that 67 out of 69 sanctioned posts for secretaries and senior secretaries are filled, while joint secretary positions see 893 officials serving against 1,116 sanctioned posts.

Across various cadres under the Public Service Commission, there are currently 8,099 vacant posts. The government has formulated six-month, one-year, and five-year action plans to fill these vacancies.
To accelerate recruitment, the Ministry of Public Administration has requested other ministries and departments to publish recruitment notices as soon as possible and prepare time-bound action plans.
The minister also noted that the time taken to publish final BCS results has been decreasing, with the goal of publishing the 50th BCS results within one year of the recruitment circular.
Additionally, Abdul Bari stated that investigations are underway to identify officials who worked to sustain the previous fascist government, and measures will be taken against them once identified.
Regarding ethics, the minister emphasized that merit, honesty, and competence are now the guiding principles for recruitment and postings, free from political influence.
caption:
Over 5.21 lakh government jobs are currently vacant in Bangladesh. Here is the government's plan to fill them.

State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari informed parliament that 521,922 government service posts remain vacant as of June 30, 2025, while 1,464,350 officials are currently in service.

The minister detailed the vacancy status across different levels, noting that 67 out of 69 sanctioned posts for secretaries and senior secretaries are filled, while joint secretary positions see 893 officials serving against 1,116 sanctioned posts.

Across various cadres under the Public Service Commission, there are currently 8,099 vacant posts. The government has formulated six-month, one-year, and five-year action plans to fill these vacancies.

To accelerate recruitment, the Ministry of Public Administration has requested other ministries and departments to publish recruitment notices as soon as possible and prepare time-bound action plans.

The minister also noted that the time taken to publish final BCS results has been decreasing, with the goal of publishing the 50th BCS results within one year of the recruitment circular.

Additionally, Abdul Bari stated that investigations are underway to identify officials who worked to sustain the previous fascist government, and measures will be taken against them once identified.

Regarding ethics, the minister emphasized that merit, honesty, and competence are now the guiding principles for recruitment and postings, free from political influence.
